context: Sakura and Naoko visit a regional craft market for inspiration.
purpose: Two adults exploring local arts together.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: さくらちゃん、ここの市、面白いやろ?
lines.en: Sakura — isn't this market something special?
lines.style: Warm, inviting Kansai lilt. Generous energy but not forced. Leans into the question like she already knows the answer and just wants to see Sakura's face light up.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、写真、ようけ取らせていただきます。
lines.en: Yes — I'm going to take so many photos.
lines.style: Genuine enthusiasm, but measured. Professional's eye at work. Quiet determination underneath the brightness — this is research, not just tourist snapshots.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 美術館も、近くにあるで。
lines.style: Casual, helpful suggestion. Kansai warmth without pressure. A small gift offered — here, take this too if you want it. The tone of someone who knows exactly what would be useful.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 記事、まだ書いてない、悲しい!
lines.en: The article — I haven't started writing it yet. It's so frustrating.
lines.style: Rueful, self-aware complaint. A small laugh underneath. She's venting to someone she trusts, and she knows Naoko will get it. The frustrated sigh of a writer staring at notes.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 徐々に、進歩しとるやんか!
lines.en: Look at you, making real progress though!
lines.style: Bright, energetic Kansai aunt brightness. A firm, affectionate correction — she's not letting Sakura spiral. The tone of someone who sees more in you than you see in yourself.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: メモだらけ、時計見ながら、書きます。
lines.en: I'll write it with my notes spread out, clock-watching the whole time.
lines.style: Wry, matter-of-fact. Accepting her own process without apology. A slight smile underneath — she's found her rhythm and she's okay with it, even if it's messy.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: お前なら、絶対できる、レス対応で。
lines.en: You've got this — no doubt about it.
lines.style: Firm, steady Kansai conviction. Low and certain, not loud. The kind of belief that doesn't need defending. She's said it plainly because she means it completely.
